title: Shift operators
context: What do the shift operators <<, >> and >>> do in Java?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (1 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `<<` shifts bits left and fills with zeros. It multiplies by 2 for each shift, as long as no sign bit changes. `>>` is an arithmetic right shift and keeps the sign by copying the top bit. `>>>` is an unsigned right shift and fills with zeros, even for negative numbers. Shift counts are masked: for `int` only the low 5 bits count, so `1 << 32` equals `1`. For `long` the mask is 6 bits.

points.title: Sign handling
points.why: `>>` keeps the sign and `>>>` always fills with zeros. Mixing them up gives wrong results for negative numbers.

points.title: Shift distance is masked
points.why: The count is taken modulo 32 for int and 64 for long, which surprises people who expect `1 << 32` to be 0.
